## 2B.5 Research Note: Lula, Brazil, 2024

**Bottom line:** I found **no credible 2024 evidence** that Lula tolerated atrocities, destabilization, or proxy abuse by allies, militias, clients, or arms recipients. Brazil had no obvious proxy-war apparatus in 2024; the closest relevant evidence is that Lula’s diplomacy and Brazil’s formal security institutions repeatedly emphasized restraint, disarmament, and civilian protection.

### Accepted claims

- **Claim:** Brazil’s 2024 security framework was explicitly non-proliferation and safeguards based, which is incompatible with proxy-style destabilization.
  - **Title:** [Tratados e regimes com reflexos para a Defesa](https://www.gov.br/defesa/pt-br/assuntos/relacoes-internacionais/foruns-internacionais-1/tratados-e-regimes)
  - **Publisher:** Ministério da Defesa
  - **Date:** Updated 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/defesa/pt-br/assuntos/relacoes-internacionais/foruns-internacionais-1/tratados-e-regimes
  - **Claim-level summary:** The page says Brazil joined the NPT, the Constitution forbids non-peaceful nuclear use, and ABACC places the program under independent safeguards. This is strong background evidence against any policy of arming proxies or tolerating destabilizing conduct.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.5`; also `1B.5`, `1B.6`, `1B.7`

- **Claim:** Lula’s government created a permanent delegation to the Conference on Disarmament in 2024.
  - **Title:** [Decreto nº 12.237, de 25 de outubro de 2024](https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_Ato2023-2026/2024/Decreto/D12237.htm)
  - **Publisher:** Presidência da República / Planalto
  - **Date:** October 25, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_Ato2023-2026/2024/Decreto/D12237.htm
  - **Claim-level summary:** The decree formalized Brazil’s permanent participation in disarmament diplomacy. That is evidence of restraint and institutional control rather than proxy cultivation or irresponsible arms transfer behavior.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.5`; also `1B.4`, `1B.6`, `1B.10`

- **Claim:** Brazil’s top security institution reaffirmed its nuclear-security architecture and disarmament commitment.
  - **Title:** [GSI/PR participa da IV Conferência Internacional sobre Segurança Física Nuclear](https://www.gov.br/gsi/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/noticias/2024/gsi-pr-participa-da-iv-conferencia-internacional-sobre-seguranca-fisica-nuclear)
  - **Publisher:** Gabinete de Segurança Institucional da Presidência da República
  - **Date:** May 21, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/gsi/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/noticias/2024/gsi-pr-participa-da-iv-conferencia-internacional-sobre-seguranca-fisica-nuclear
  - **Claim-level summary:** Brazil’s delegation reaffirmed the national nuclear-security architecture and support for complete nuclear disarmament. This supports a pattern of restraint and formal oversight, not proxy conduct.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.5`; also `1B.4`, `1B.6`, `1B.7`

- **Claim:** Brazil maintained active IAEA cooperation in 2024.
  - **Title:** [IAEA recognizes CNEN's "crucial" role in nuclear technology development in Brazil](https://www.gov.br/cnen/pt-br/assunto/ultimas-noticias/aiea-reconhece-papel-crucial-da-cnen-no-desenvolvimento-da-tecnologia-nuclear-no-brasil)
  - **Publisher:** Comissão Nacional de Energia Nuclear
  - **Date:** June 24, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/cnen/pt-br/assunto/ultimas-noticias/aiea-reconhece-papel-crucial-da-cnen-no-desenvolvimento-da-tecnologia-nuclear-no-brasil
  - **Claim-level summary:** CNEN said IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi emphasized Brazil’s indispensable cooperation and ongoing collaboration. This is consistent with responsible stewardship rather than foreseeable proxy misuse.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.5`; also `1B.3`, `1B.4`, `1B.7`

- **Claim:** Brazil accepted IAEA self-assessment in 2024, signaling review and accountability.
  - **Title:** [Brazil participates in unprecedented IAEA self-assessment in Vienna, contributing to strengthening global nuclear safety](https://www.gov.br/cnen/pt-br/assunto/ultimas-noticias/brasil-participa-de-autoavaliacao-inedita-da-aiea-em-viena-contribuindo-para-o-fortalecimento-da-seguranca-global)
  - **Publisher:** Comissão Nacional de Energia Nuclear
  - **Date:** October 3, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/cnen/pt-br/assunto/ultimas-noticias/brasil-participa-de-autoavaliacao-inedita-da-aiea-em-viena-contribuindo-para-o-fortalecimento-da-seguranca-global
  - **Claim-level summary:** Participation in IAEA self-assessment suggests Brazil was willing to submit its nuclear governance to external review. That is the opposite of tolerating hidden proxy conduct.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.5`; also `1B.3`, `1B.7`

- **Claim:** Brazil joined a Gaza statement demanding ceasefire, hostage release, and humanitarian aid.
  - **Title:** [Brasil assina declaração conjunta pelo fim dos ataques sobre Gaza](https://agenciagov.ebc.com.br/noticias/202406/declaracao-conjunta-sobre-gaza)
  - **Publisher:** Agência Gov / MRE
  - **Date:** June 6, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://agenciagov.ebc.com.br/noticias/202406/declaracao-conjunta-sobre-gaza
  - **Claim-level summary:** The declaration called for hostilities to stop, hostages to be released, and humanitarian aid to reach civilians. This is the clearest direct evidence of Lula-aligned restraint toward civilian harm and destabilization.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.5`; also `2B.4`, `2B.1`

- **Claim:** Lula repeatedly described the Ukraine and Gaza crises in peace-oriented terms rather than as proxy arenas.
  - **Title:** [Lula said he discussed peace in Ukraine and Gaza with Antony Blinken](https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/02/21/lula-diz-que-discutiu-conflitos-em-gaza-e-na-ucrania-em-encontro-com-blinken.htm)
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL
  - **Date:** February 21, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/02/21/lula-diz-que-discutiu-conflitos-em-gaza-e-na-ucrania-em-encontro-com-blinken.htm
  - **Claim-level summary:** Lula said he discussed peace in Ukraine and Gaza with Antony Blinken, and Planalto reiterated his desire for peace and an end to the conflicts. This supports restraint rather than proxy escalation.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.5`; also `1B.8`, `2B.1`

### Counterevidence / caveats

- **Claim:** Lula’s Gaza rhetoric was confrontational and caused a diplomatic rupture, but it still was not proxy enabling.
  - **Title:** [Lula repeats that the Israeli government commits genocide in Gaza and defends the creation of a Palestinian state](https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/02/23/lula-repete-que-governo-israelense-comete-genocidio-em-gaza-e-defende-criacao-de-estado-palestino.htm)
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL
  - **Date:** February 23, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/02/23/lula-repete-que-governo-israelense-comete-genocidio-em-gaza-e-defende-criacao-de-estado-palestino.htm
  - **Claim-level summary:** Lula repeated the genocide accusation and defended Palestinian statehood, triggering a diplomatic rupture with Israel. This is the main negative item, but it is rhetoric, not evidence of Lula accepting responsibility for proxy atrocities.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.5`; also `1B.2`, `1B.8`

### Search gap

I found **no direct 2024 evidence** that Lula:
- armed proxies or clients,
- tolerated militia atrocities,
- failed to restrain allied forces,
- or knowingly accepted foreseeable proxy conduct.

That is partly because Brazil was not operating as a proxy sponsor in 2024. The evidence base is therefore mostly indirect, but it points consistently toward restraint, oversight, and humanitarian language rather than proxy-enabled abuse.
